subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type, TPS targets, and token mix
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type, TPS targets, and token mix

Hi Chris / Morgan —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap + a few follow-up questions so our sizing recommendation is targeted:

Call recap (TL;DR):
- Workload: multi-turn summarization + long-form generation for customer support tickets and internal analytics pipelines.
- Current traffic: spiky during business hours; you mentioned a peak of ~50 TPS for inference (user-facing calls) and ~10k batched embedding requests overnight.
- Requirements: <100ms p95 user latency target for short-path queries; otherwise tactical slack for async jobs.

Follow-ups we need to size Dedicated properly:
1) Confirm peak TPS and spike duration: is 50 TPS sustained for >10 minutes or multiple short bursts?
2) Token mix: please confirm average prompt tokens and average completion tokens. In our call you said ~120 prompt tokens and ~350 completion tokens on average — is that accurate?
3) Concurrency expectation: how many concurrent user requests at peak should we budget for? You mentioned ~20 concurrent.
4) Preferred GPU family: do you have preference for H100 vs A100, or budget constraint that would push toward cheaper options? We can size for either and show cost delta.

If the numbers above are correct (50 TPS peak, 20 concurrency, 120/350 token mix) we can propose a Dedicated pool with mixed H100/A100 nodes and suggestions for KV caching and quantization (4-bit) to lower costs while meeting latency SLOs.

Attached: please drop the usage export if you have one (acme-metrics.csv helps).

Next steps: if you can confirm the three bullets (peak sustained duration, precise token averages, concurrency target) I’ll loop in Marissa (SE) to draft a sizing doc and cost estimate and we can book a 30m follow-up next week.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hey Dylan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming details below:

- Peak TPS: 50 TPS is correct for user-facing generation. Typically spikes last ~3–12 minutes and can occur several times per hour during the 9am–5pm PT window. We see a longer sustained surge (20–30 minutes) during batch processing after our morning data refresh.
- Token mix: prompt avg ~130 tokens (range 80–220), completion avg ~360 tokens (range 100–1200 for long-form).
- Concurrency: expecting ~20 parallel user-facing live requests at peak. Additionally, we run concurrent batch jobs (embeddings) that are isolated to a different queue — they can be throttled to non-peak hours.
- GPU preference: open to both. We prefer H100 for headroom on complex long-form renders but would like A100 cost comparisons. If Dedicated can autoscale with burst to H100 for peaks, that’d be ideal.

I attached the export (acme-metrics.csv) showing recent traffic — hope it helps.

cc: Morgan — any edits?

Cheers,
Chris Evans
Principal ML Engineer, Acme Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-02-23T11:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU type, TPS targets, and token mix

Hi Chris —

Thanks for the details and the CSV — very helpful. Quick technical read and sizing notes based on the stated workload (50 TPS peaks with 20 concurrency, avg token mix ~130/360):

Sizing guidance (initial):
- GPU options: 1) H100 (80GB gated) will give the best p95 latency headroom for long-form cases. 2) A100 (40GB) is doable with 4-bit quantization for most requests; expect ~20–30% higher latency on worst-case long completions.
- Baseline nodes: For steady-state 50 TPS mixed profile we estimate ~4 x A100 (40GB) nodes with optimized batching and KV caching to meet p95 ~80–120ms for short responses and ~200–400ms for typical long-form completions.
- Peak/Headroom: If you want single-digit p95 under heavy long-form load, consider 2 x H100 nodes in a burst pool + 4 x A100 baseline.
- Concurrency and batching: budget for 20 concurrent active requests; configure per-model concurrency limits and per-instance batching windows (10–20ms) to avoid latency spikes. Continuous batching will help with throughput but we keep per-request jitter low with small windows.
- Token throughput: with avg 490 tokens/request (prompt+completion) and 50 TPS, that's ~24.5k tokens/sec peak. That affects memory/KV cache sizing — we recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated context across conversations.

Tradeoffs and recommendations:
- Cost vs latency: A100 baseline + H100 burst is a good cost/latency compromise.
- Quantization: 4-bit quantization provides ~2x memory savings; we'd like to run evals on a representative prompt set (we can use your export) to validate quality.
- Private VPC/on-prem: if you require network isolation, we can size similarly but add buffer for on-prem throughput variability.

Deliverables I’ll produce once we confirm traffic:
- Detailed node-by-node cost and latency projection (A100 baseline vs H100 baseline vs hybrid)
- Suggested autoscale policy (CPU/GPU queue length + scheduled burst)
- Eval plan to validate 4-bit quality impact against your prompt set

Next step: Dylan / Chris — can we lock a 30m slot next Wed (2026-02-25) for a walkthrough of the sizing doc? I’ll attach a draft map (draft-map.pdf) with node counts and autoscale triggers for your review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
